definition: Image translation is the machine translation of images of printed text (posters, banners, menus, screenshots etc.).
details: This is done by applying optical character recognition (OCR) technology to an image to extract any text contained in the image, and then have this text translated into a language of their choice, and the applying digital image processing on the original image to get the translated image with a new language.

explainer.lead: Image translation means machine-translating the printed text inside an image, such as a poster, menu or screenshot. It matters because it lets users read foreign-language text in real screenshots and photos without retyping it.

tiers.eli5: It's like holding a camera up to a foreign menu and getting the same menu back with the words in your language.
tiers.practitioner: The pipeline runs OCR to extract text, translates it, then edits the original image to place the translated text. A frequent pitfall is that reinserted text overflows or misaligns where the original wording had different length.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is composed of OCR text extraction, machine translation, and digital image processing to render translated text into the original image. Limits come from OCR errors on stylized text and layout constraints on the re-rendered result.

explainer.example: A screenshot of a foreign-language banner is OCR'd, its text translated, and the banner re-rendered with the translated wording in place.
